attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: Revision 2 uses the verbatim sentence and keeps the 'outside of coding' scope and the three named exceptions. It is a firm, unhedged statement about the present.

contract.note: The speaker did not define 'fundamental'. Reading it as substantive, repeatable practical use rather than demos or anecdotes is an ordinary plain reading. Limiting AI to generative AI matches the LLM context. Treating a single counterexample as enough fits the sweeping 'no fundamental use cases'.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed randomized implementation, published Nov 2025, before the post. LLM ambient scribes cut note time by about 0.36 h/day without loss of note quality. Clinical note drafting falls outside coding, search interpretation, brainstorming and document search.
Sponsor's registry record. Confirms the intervention used LLMs and the study finished in March 2025. Supports how e1 is classified and dated.
A different LLM application: decision support in Kenya, which missed its primary outcome. Does not cancel the documentation result.

reviews.rationale: Before July 2026, a peer-reviewed randomized deployment showed an LLM application outside the listed exceptions (clinical note generation) giving a measured practical benefit: less documentation time with quality kept. That meets the contract's contradiction condition. e3 limits wider claims about clinical effectiveness but does not negate this use.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the main assertion: no shown sustainable GPU-rental model, and no profits justifying the debt. Dropping the rhetorical 'payoff date' aside is fine because it sets no deadline.

contract.note: Defining sustainability as rental economics that cover operating costs, replacement and debt service is an ordinary reading. Using Q1 2026 as the window is the evaluator's choice but reasonable. The operator population is undefined, and the support condition requires comprehensive records.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's own disclosure for Q1 2026: $144M operating loss, $740M net loss, and $536M net interest against $21M adjusted operating income. It shows no debt coverage at this operator. The quoted backlog figure shows demand, not profit.
Nebius's own Q1 2026 disclosure: a $128M operating loss. Its net income came from an investment revaluation gain, not from rental profits.

reviews.rationale: The two leading specialist operators both posted operating losses in Q1 2026, which leans toward the claim. But the support condition needs representative, comprehensive operator records, and evidence that separates rental cash generation from replacement and debt service. Two company disclosures do not meet that, so the packet does not settle a sector-wide negative.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Captures the widening and the repayment-concern reading. The '540 to 756bps' figures and the 'last month' window are kept in the threshold and the contract.

contract.note: Reading the claim as a substantial selloff with more repayment risk priced in, not as a default prediction, is fair. Requiring matched OAS observations for the same June 2026 dollar notes is appropriate.

evidence.note: Issuer's pricing notice identifies the $1.25B 9.625% 2032 notes, issued at par on June 11, 2026. It contains no OAS observations at issuance or later.

reviews.rationale: The packet identifies the bond but has no dated OAS or price data for issuance or late July, and no credit analysis of the selling or of repayment concern. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition can be checked.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the 5.6% of 7.1GW figure, 'currently', and the June 2026 start. Dropping the 'burning to the ground' rhetoric and the deal value is acceptable; the contract treats them as background.

contract.note: Testing operational capacity on the same power basis as the 7.1GW denominator, plus the intended start date, is a fair reading. The power basis and the July window are evaluator choices, and both are flagged.

evidence.note: Sept 2025 news report, citing the WSJ, says purchases would start in 2027. This conflicts with June 2026, but it is secondhand and predates the target period, so it does not establish the contract terms.
Secondary summary, dated before the cutoff. Puts Abilene at 421MW of IT load in July 2026. That covers one site only, with no matching 7.1GW denominator or total across the customer's capacity.
OpenAI's July 2025 announcement of a 4.5GW development deal. Does not verify 7.1GW or the July 2026 operating share.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no total of operational Oracle–OpenAI capacity on a basis consistent with 7.1GW, and no contract record of the start date. The Abilene figure alone is near the implied 398MW but uses a different scope. The report of a 2027 start conflicts with June 2026 but is secondhand. Nothing settles the claim.
